how: We read the website of every Indianapolis wedding photographer listed on Lazo (99 listings, 64 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: a national franchise with an Indianapolis landing page, a Fort Wayne studio with an Indy page, senior, family and newborn portrait studios, a headshot and corporate shooter, and a 24-hour content-creation service. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: Can I see a full gallery from a wedding at a venue like mine, including getting ready and the reception, not just portraits?
Is a second shooter included, and what is the delivery timeline for the full gallery?
If the day is grey and cold, or a July ceremony is in full sun, how do you handle the light? Ask for examples of both.

picks.name: Sara Ackermann Photography
picks.blurb: A decade of weddings from an Indy-raised photographer who describes herself as a lifestyle and wedding shooter working across the US with an office in Indianapolis. Sara prints one wedding package at $5,750 that includes eight hours of coverage, with add-ons to customize it.

picks.name: Stacy Able Photography
picks.blurb: Honest, editorial wedding photography for modern couples, in Stacy's words, with over 500 celebrations behind her and a 17th year in business. Based in Indianapolis, she serves couples of all faiths and orientations, hand-edits every image, and offers drone imagery and elopement coverage as extras.

picks.name: Amanda DeBusk Photography
picks.blurb: An inclusive, queer-friendly wedding and elopement photographer who has been behind the lens since 2012 and photographed hundreds of couples. Amanda shoots fun-yet-romantic, clean, classic images at everything from elopements and backyard weddings to parties that go all night.

picks.name: Clay House Photography
picks.blurb: A team of Indianapolis documentary wedding photographers that grew out of one founder shooting solo, who then built an associate team to serve more couples and budgets. Clay House tells you its first wedding paid $60 and a Finish Line gift card, which is the kind of candor the site runs on.

picks.name: Rogue Image Photo
picks.blurb: Documentary-style wedding photography from McCordsville, described as clean, crisp and timeless, for elopements through grand weddings in Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville and across Central Indiana. Rogue Image publishes a pricing page that answers what a wedding photographer costs in Indianapolis, and says everyone is welcome.

picks.name: Monica Brown Photography
picks.blurb: A husband-and-wife team based in Indianapolis who specialize in destination weddings. Monica is the lead photographer and primary contact, Drew is the second shooter, tech support and business manager, and they met the first week of college at Miami of Ohio through a campus ministry.

picks.name: Ralph Vandale Photography And Videography LLC
picks.blurb: Artistic, editorial wedding photos and films with a luxury pitch: Ralph Vandale promises magazine-worthy moments and iconic portraits, and cites over seven years of experience, celebrity work and features in bridal publications. Photo and film from one Indianapolis studio.

picks.name: Sandhu wedding photography
picks.blurb: Over 20 years of Indian wedding photography, with a stated understanding of culture and tradition and a vibrant, cinematic storytelling style. Sandhu covers Indian and Punjabi weddings, pre-wedding and engagement shoots and destination work from New Whiteland, with cinematography as well.

picks.name: Kumar Wedding Photography
picks.blurb: A Sikh, Punjabi and South Asian wedding photographer and videographer based in Indiana, also covering Pakistani weddings, pre-weddings, portraits and events, and often travelling to the destination. Kumar's pitch is real people and real stories rather than posed pictures.

picks.name: Kirsten Wray Photography
picks.blurb: Luxury wedding and portrait photography from Fishers, led by founder Kirsten with over 20 years of experience and storytelling as the stated heart of every shoot. KWP also photographs families and brands, so expect a studio that works beyond wedding season.

picks.name: DL Photography Studio
picks.blurb: Danielle in Greenwood pitches bold, vibrant photos for couples who laugh too loud and love too hard, and says she is not your typical photographer, which is the point. Services include timeline creating, so the day gets planned as well as photographed.

picks.name: Marissa Wiley Photo
picks.blurb: Marissa's collections bundle more than the day: a wedding consult, planning assistance and vendor recommendations, a customized timeline, an engagement session, wedding-day coverage and an online gallery. She describes a personalized experience for couples who value one, from Indianapolis.
